newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds creep higher in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds creep higher in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities barely budged higher in light trade on Friday, and yield spreads to comparable Treasuries tightened by a whisker, traders said.
"Yield spreads narrowed fractionally, but certainly that didn't draw much attention," said one Ginnie trader.
With little economic data to lend the market direction, many market participants were inactive, leaving mortgage-backed instruments stuck in a narrow band, he said.
"(Traders) were scratching for little bits and pieces, but not too many were getting them," another trader said. "It's like mid-summer dead, when everybody goes on vacation," he added.
By late afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 3/32 at 100-25/32 bid, yielding 98 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was up 2/32 at 100-19/32 bid, and Freddie Mac issues inched up 1/32 at 100-23/32 bid.
The five-year Treasury note was up 1/32 to yield 6.28 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was up 4/32 to yield 6.38 percent.
